text: The Kunming Metro, also known as Kunming Rail Transit, is a rapid transit system serving Kunming, the capital of China's Yunnan Province. The system currently comprises 6 operational lines, with 2 extensions to existing lines under construction and 3 additional lines planned, totaling 164.3 kilometers of track. Due to long-standing traffic congestion in Kunming's streets, discussions about a subway system have existed since the late 1990s. At the time of construction, the city had a population of just over 3 million, with the built-up urban area reaching over 5 million by 2020, making it one of the largest Chinese cities without a metro system prior to development. A 2006 proposal suggested starting construction in 2008 with a north-south and east-west line, while the current system was first announced in 2009, with construction beginning later that year. The metro was designed not only to relieve traffic in the city center but also to promote development in the southeast, particularly in the Chenggong District, which experienced a construction boom despite lacking adequate transit links. Construction on Lines 1 and 2 began officially in May 2010, after delays, with an elevated test section having been built since 2009. Lines 1 (34 km) and 2 (22 km) were initially scheduled for opening in 2012 but were delayed and opened in early 2013. Line 3 began construction in August 2010 and opened on 29 August 2017. The construction of Line 1 was estimated to cost up to 32 billion yuan (US$4.5 billion), with elevated sections costing around 250 million yuan per kilometer and underground sections ranging from 400 to 800 million yuan per kilometer; China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) is the primary contractor. Line 6 trains were manufactured by China South Locomotive & Rolling Stock Corporation Ltd (CSR, now CRRC) in Zhuzhou and operate as 6-car sets at 120 km/h; CSR discussed safety concerns related to these speeds in October 2011. Rolling stock has been updated over time: Line 1, 2, and 6 feature LED physical route maps, with some Line 1 and 2 trains upgraded to digital UIs; Line 3 uses a digital route map with a basic UI; Line 4 has darker flooring, a new info board UI, and a remade route map UI; Line 5 reverted to white flooring, updated its info board and route map UIs, and features projectors on the exterior that display advertisements on tunnel walls. Line 1 is 33.3 km long with 22 stations, running from South Ring Road to University Town (South) and Kunming South Railway Station, and currently has through service with Line 2, which will end when Line 1 Northwest Extension and Line 2 Phase 2 open, turning South Ring Road into an interchange. The first phase of Line 1 opened on 20 May 2013, the second phase on 30 April 2014, and a 5.3 km branch to Kunming South Railway Station opened on 26 December 2016. Line 1 includes an elevated section connecting Kunming to Chenggong and an underground section beneath Caiyun Road in Chenggong, with the northwest extension planned to be dug underground along the west side of the city center, serving as Kunming’s main rail link to Chenggong. Line 1’s color is red. Line 2 is 12.4 km long with 14 stations, running from North Coach Station to South Ring Road, and shares through service with Line 1, which will end when Line 2 Phase 2 opens, extending its route to Haidong Park. The first phase opened on 30 April 2014; the route includes a short elevated section to Longtou Street and an underground section beneath Beijing Road to South Ring Road. Phase 2 will be dug beneath Guannan Avenue and Fubao Road toward Haidong Park, making it Kunming’s main north-south line. Line 2’s color is blue. Line 3, which opened on 29 August 2017, is 19.16 km long with 20 stations, running from Western Hills Park to East Coach Station, and serves as Kunming’s main east-west line; its color is magenta. Line 4, which began operations on 23 September 2020, is 43.4 km long with 29 stations, running from Jinchuan Road to Kunming South Railway Station, connecting Northwest and Eastern Kunming to the metro and serving as a second link to Chenggong; it features cartoon mascots known as the "K4 Cats" to promote ridership; its color is orange. Line 5, which started on 29 June 2022, is 26.5 km long with 22 stations, running from World Horti-Expo Garden to Baofeng, and functions as a tourism line linking destinations such as World Horti-Expo Garden, Haigeng Great Dam, and Haigeng Park; its color is green. Line 6, 25.3 km long with 8 stations, runs from Kunming Airport to Tangzixiang; Phase 1 opened on 28 June 2012, and Phase 2 opened on 23 September 2020, extending it to Tangzixiang just south of the city center. It is an airport express line connecting the city center with Kunming Changshui International Airport; its original terminus at East Coach Station was not connected to other lines until Line 3 opened in 2017, and the two intermediate stations between East Coach Station and Kunming Airport were built as infill stations. Line 6 temporarily ceased operations on 5 March 2016 to complete the infill stations and resumed on 29 August 2017 with four stations; its color is teal. Extensions of Lines 1 and 2 are under construction but have faced delays, originally projected for 2022 and now expected to open in December 2026. Line 9 (Songming Line) and the Anning Line are planned, with all phase 1 station names confirmed. However, construction of the planned new lines is currently on hold due to a lack of funding and unstable leadership.
